research_scope: Source-free mathematical prerequisite identity audit against original formulation text; parent scope and stronger structural conditions remain distinct.

aliases.reason: For irreducible components of Spec(R), p is a prime ideal minimal under inclusion among primes; the geometrically irreducible algebra source counts the same minimal prime ideals after scalar extension. The shared prerequisite is minimal prime under inclusion, and no hypotheses about geometrical irreducibility or component uniqueness are transferred.

The filtered-category source requires a pair of parallel arrows u,v:i⇉j that become equal after an outgoing morphism, and the equalizer source starts with parallel f,g:X⇉Y. They both use the same typed notion: two arrows with exactly matching source and target. Subsequent equalizing maps and respective universal properties remain different.

The representable-presheaf-morphism source identifies ξ∈G(U) with a Yoneda natural transformation h_U→G; its prerequisite is an ordinary natural transformation between presheaves, already specified by commuting naturality squares. The Yoneda construction is a distinguished instance, and the fibre-product and representability requirements remain parent-specific.

The connected-limit/colimit source references a diagram with a connected indexing category; the ordinary diagram prerequisite is the functor D:I→C. Its context explicitly takes I small, a source-specific indexing restriction. It does not impose smallness on arbitrary C or identify connected diagrams with general diagrams as parent notions.

Finite limit/colimit sources invoke a diagram F:I→C where the index category has finitely many objects and morphisms. This is the general diagram-as-functor construction, specialized to finite and hence small indexing I; the finite index restriction and target locally-small convention remain source-specific.
